what_it_shows: Ocado Meat & Poultry: categories Beef, Butcher's Counter, Chicken, Pork, Lamb (species first); brand and dietary filters
USDA carcass beef quality grades Prime/Choice/Select/Standard/Commercial/Utility/Cutter/Canner by marbling+maturity; yield grades 1-5
Beef collection by cut (entrecote, faux-filet, onglet, picanha, hache) with breed (Angus, Simmental), halal and maturation as attributes

Real Decreto 4/2014 quality standard for ibérico meat, ham, shoulder, loin: sale name = feeding (bellota, cebo de campo, cebo) x breed (100% ibérico, ibérico 50/75%); colour seals black/red/green/white; 'pata negra' reserved

MAFF Japanese Beef Products guide: Wagyu = four breeds born and raised in Japan; JMGA grade = yield A-C x quality 1-5 (15 grades, lowest of four factors); primal and retail cuts (chuck roll, shoulder clod, ribloin, sirloin, short plate, knuckle...)
JMGA A5/A4/A3 vs BMS 1-12 marbling bands; Australian MB and USDA scales not comparable; grade is carcass-level
Interbev/Inaporc cut posters per species (beef, veal, lamb, kid, offal, horse, pork); cuts grouped by culinary destination and cooking type
AHDB Meat Purchasing Guide (700+ cuts of beef, lamb, pork, mutton, veal) and per-species yield guides carcase to primal to cut
French vs UK beef cut names grouped steaks/roasting/stewing; same cut sold or cooked differently; pork and lamb similar in both
Chinese pork part names mapped to US names (pork belly, Boston butt/collar, tenderloin, jowl, hock, trotter...)
GB/T 9959.3-2019 national standard for fresh and frozen pork cuts (part of a 4-part series: demi-carcass, lean cuts, cuts, by-products)

D'Artagnan facets: Type mixes species, breed, feeding, grade, origin and charcuterie (Angus, Japanese A5, Berkshire, Grass-Fed, Bison, Boar, Venison, Bacon, Duck Charcuterie); Cut facet; Bone/Skin; Fresh/Frozen; Cooking Method; Portion Type; Brand
Crowd Cow beef: first split by feeding (Pasture-Raised, 100% Grass Fed), then Butcher's Cuts (steak list), ranch/farm, cooking method, occasion

Japanese meat wholesaler: Beef (cut-led incl. wagyu/domestic/imported), Pork (branded 銘柄豚, Iberico, black pork), Chicken (regional brand 地鶏), Other (lamb, duck, horse, venison, rabbit, pigeon, quail), Processed (prosciutto, coppa, mortadella, chorizo)
Japan Food Labeling Standard definitions: ham (bone-in, boneless, loin, shoulder, belly, lax), bacon, press ham, sausage types (dry, semi-dry, cooked, liver, bologna, frankfurter, wiener)
Beef parts: MAFF retail labelling 9 parts; trade-standard 13 parts (adds neck, shin; belly and round split); rare cuts sit under them
Guidelines for meat and meat products: sausages split Rohwurst/Bruehwurst/Kochwurst, cured raw (Rohpoekelwaren) and cooked cured (Kochpoekelwaren) meats, Spitzenqualitaet claim rules, GI annex
HS/CN Chapter 02 headings: bovine, swine, sheep-goat, horse, offal, poultry, other meat, fat, and salted-dried-smoked (0210); fresh vs frozen split

Poultry marketing standard: species (fowl, turkey, duck, goose, guinea fowl), carcase types (capon, poussin), cuts, classes A/B, farming terms (free range, traditional free range, total freedom) with minimum ages

Spanish online butcher: sells by species/cut (chuletones, entrecots, solomillo, cerdo y cochinillo, lechazo, ibericos) with own three-grade scheme extra/select/top, seals (Classic, Wagyu, Deluxe, Angus Beef) and dry-aged maturation

Spanish gourmet shop: Gran Carniceria (ternera, cerdo, pollo, cerdo iberico), Gran Charcuteria (fiambres, embutidos al corte), Jamoneria (iberico vs serrano hams and shoulders), Embutidos Ibericos (sliced, whole, half)
Hanwoo quality grades 1++/1+/1/2/3 by marbling percentage plus yield grade A/B/C; not equivalent to Japanese A5
Steak buying guide: cut, grade, marbling and packaging; aged 14 to 30 days; ask butcher (page text partly paywalled)
Pork breed comparison table: Kurobuta/Berkshire, Duroc, Iberico, Chester White, Tamworth, Large Black by marbling, flavor and price tier
Eight US beef primals (chuck, rib, loin, round, flank, plate, brisket, shank) with sub-primals, portion cuts and carcass percentages
New national beef grading GB/T 29392-2026: beef first classed S (lean) or F (fat type), then grades 1-4, by maturity, meat colour, fat colour, intramuscular fat; in force 2026-12-01
Game category by species: venison, pheasant, partridge, wood pigeon, hare, wild boar, duck, rabbit, squirrel
Charcuterie tree: saucissons and dry sausages, hams, dried meat, cured meat, nitrite-free, terrines/rillettes/potted meat (duck, game, poultry)
French charcuterie families: pate, terrine, mousse, rillettes, boudin, saucisson, jambon (page body mostly not returned)
Chinese-language cut guide mapping North American primals to Chinese names (板腱, 翼板, 牛腩, 牛腱, 肋眼, 老饕, 戰斧, 紐約客, 菲力, 沙朗, 牛五花)
